The account is fixed when a session starts. A personal session already running won't change, and new sessions follow whichever folder they start in.

=================== README.md
# Discourse Graphs Review Lab

> **Alpha. LLM-created. Not yet tested in real team use.** This project attempts
> to accurately represent the current workflow used to review Discourse
> Graphs PRs. That workflow is constantly in flux. This package is an evolving
> draft, not an established team process or a guarantee of review correctness.

Automated synthetic checks have been run. They are recorded separately in
[Testing](docs/testing.md) and do not establish teammate, macOS or live-provider
acceptance. The alpha status applies even when automated checks pass.

This private repository packages DG PR triage, pinned detailed reviews, changed-head
refreshes and offline HTML. It keeps one shared assessment record and renderer.
Local review progress is separate from GitHub approval. Provider collection is
read-only and limited to the configured repository in the DiscourseGraphs organization.
The example target is `DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph`; DG Roam and Obsidian clients
remain legitimate review surfaces.

## Start with synthetic data

Use Python 3.11+ (`python3` on macOS). No provider access is needed:

```sh
python scripts/team_review.py sample
```

Open `local/synthetic/index.html`. The example is synthetic DG-shaped data, not a
real PR snapshot. Read [TEAM-INSTALL.md](TEAM-INSTALL.md) for configuration,
authentication, operation, updates and cleanup. The repository source is
`https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/review-lab`.

To preview concrete before/after explanations without provider access:

```sh
python skills/mg-review-lab/scripts/review_lab.py render --input examples/narratives.json --output local/narratives/index.html
```

Open `local/narratives/index.html`, choose either synthetic PR and expand
“The change, explained.” These examples show a published field moving and a
reader's field preference changing, with pseudocode and local diff jumps.

## Use with Codex

Read [mg-review-lab](skills/mg-review-lab/SKILL.md) and supply an explicit local
configuration. The skill routes queue refresh, targeted review, saved prioritization
and HTML rendering. A complete refresh includes fresh evidence and assessment of
every changed/new snapshot. Collection or re-rendering alone is not a code review.

Keep real PR records, source evidence, notes, credentials and local configuration in
ignored `local/` or a private output directory. Do not commit them. Cloning does not
install global skills, profile commands, schedulers or services. No review submission,
comment posting, automated fixes, merging or deployments are included.

## Included

- Configurable reviewer, DG repository, evidence paths and stable localhost port.
- Detached inspection, immutable diff pins and source evidence retained after cleanup.
- Intent/scope assessment, findings/checks, Guided walkthroughs and optional Shape maps.
- Shared offline renderer, local notes/progress and matching-snapshot state transfer.
- Concrete change examples and before/after pseudocode, with legacy narrative support.
- DG-only collector guards and synthetic regression tests.

See [architecture](docs/architecture.md), [portability](docs/portability.md),
[provenance](docs/provenance.md) and [roadmap](ROADMAP.md).

# DG alpha installation and operation

Alpha, LLM-created, not yet tested in real team use. This evolving package attempts
to reflect the current DG review workflow, which is constantly in flux.
Canonical DG source: https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/review-lab (private).
Automated synthetic checks are documented separately in docs/testing.md.

## Required tools and access

| Operation | Requirements |
| --- | --- |
| Synthetic rendering, saved HTML, local server | Python 3.11+, browser; standard library only |
| Requested-PR discovery and pinned preparation | Git, authenticated GitHub CLI (`gh`), repository read access |
| Intent assessment | Linear read connector or supplied dated issue/comments/spec evidence |
| DG review prose | Configured target checkout's `.agents/skills/dg-engineering-writing-style/SKILL.md` |
| Optional Shape maps | Node.js 18+, pinned TypeScript 5.5.4; follow `docs/shape.md` |
| Product verification | Target repository instructions and its toolchain; package tests do not replace them |

Credentials stay in GitHub CLI / connector stores. Do not put tokens, raw provider
evidence or local paths in committed configuration. A teammate needs access to the
private canonical repository; granting access or moving ownership requires a team
decision. No account permissions were changed by this draft.

# PR Review HTML

Create a read-only, evidence-based PR review. Never change GitHub state, the PR branch, or the active worktree. Never launch a nested `codex` process.

## Workflow

1. Use `dg-engineering-writing-style` from the owning Discourse Graph repository for all review prose. For the portable team pilot, resolve and verify its explicit `writing_skill` configuration through [team setup](../mg-review-lab/references/team-setup.md). If the skill is unavailable, report the missing dependency; do not substitute a personal writing style.
2. Confirm the PR belongs to the current DiscourseGraphs repository. Non-DG targets are rejected.
3. Prepare a detached worktree from the repository root. Checkouts live under `<repository>/local/reviews/.worktrees/<run>/worktree`; manifests, JSON, and retrieved context live under `local/reviews/.runs/<run>/`. Both are locally ignored:

```powershell
python "<package>/skills/mg-pr-review-html/scripts/generate_pr_review.py" prepare --pr 123
```

Add `--linear-ticket ENG-1855` when the request names a ticket. Omit `--pr` only when the current branch has a PR. Preparation otherwise searches the PR description, then the first three PR comments for a Linear reference. Inspect other relevant links in PR metadata and retrieved context.

4. Read the printed manifest, generated instructions, and schema completely.
5. If a Linear candidate was discovered, retrieve the full issue and every comment with the connected Linear read tools. Follow comment pagination. Read directly relevant linked tickets, scope/spec docs, and design decisions. Save retrieved material in `run_dir/context/`; put source metadata and requirement assessments in the review JSON. Record inaccessible or conflicting sources. Never update Linear or external documents.
6. Review only the manifest's pinned base-to-head diff in its detached worktree. Inspect surrounding code and run proportionate checks.
7. Write one JSON object at `review_json` that exactly matches the schema.
8. Finalize the review:

```powershell
python "<package>/skills/mg-pr-review-html/scripts/generate_pr_review.py" finalize --manifest <manifest-path>
```

Finalization always removes the temporary worktree unless preparation used
`--keep-worktree`. If the review JSON is invalid, it preserves the small run artifacts
for correction but still removes the worktree. A later `prepare` also reaps abandoned,
non-retained worktrees from runs older than 12 hours.

9. Report every generated HTML path. Open a page only when asked.

## Worktree maintenance

Run these from the repository root using the same `generate_pr_review.py` script:

```powershell
python "<package>/skills/mg-pr-review-html/scripts/generate_pr_review.py" list
python "<package>/skills/mg-pr-review-html/scripts/generate_pr_review.py" cleanup --stale --dry-run
python "<package>/skills/mg-pr-review-html/scripts/generate_pr_review.py" cleanup --stale
```

Use `cleanup --all` for all non-retained runs, or `--pr 123` to narrow a batch. `--dry-run` prints paths without removal. Batch cleanup skips `--keep-worktree` runs; clean a retained run explicitly with `--manifest <path>`. Run artifacts are preserved by default. Add `--remove-artifacts` to remove that run's JSON/context too; rendered HTML remains.

Older version 2 manifests still support cleanup of their exact system-temp checkouts. Cleanup does not scan/delete arbitrary temp folders. Failed Git removal and unregistered directories containing files are preserved for inspection, with an actionable path. Use the Git-aware cleanup command rather than deleting a registered worktree in Explorer.

## Review contract

- Apply `references/codex-review-rubric.md` as the authoritative finding rubric. Only its output shape is replaced by `assets/review-output-schema.json` (version 2).
- Report actionable problems introduced by the PR. Keep findings diff-anchored, with evidence and a practical correction. Requirements reference finding IDs instead of repeating the bug.
- Organize the page around behavioral change, intent and evidence, reviewer attention, and one ordered walkthrough. Omit empty sections. Do not generate separate changed-area summaries, review maps, or beginner lessons.
- Prefer visual explanations when they reduce reading: multiple complementary visuals are welcome. Choose graph/architecture, state, sequence, decision table, before/after pseudocode, or actual UI screenshots. Follow [visual guidance](references/visual-explanations.md). Do not force a diagram for a trivial change or repeat the same explanation in several formats.
- Derive requirements from retrieved tickets/specs, not the implementation. Distinguish implementation assessment from verification. Cite sources and pinned code; link exact checks by ID. Show source conflicts and unexpected scope as explicit reviewer decisions.
- Keep review findings and verification status separate. Failed checks, unrun checks, unverified requirements, and missing intent context remain visible near the header even when no blocking bug was found.
- Use one sentence for the change summary. Short prose and concrete examples are preferred; no bullet quotas. Keep walkthrough items focused on one behavior with a reason to inspect it.
- Background and quizzes are opt-in for an explicit learning request. `learning` and `quiz` are optional and collapsed; no fixed question count.
- Wrap identifiers, paths, fields, and commands in backticks. Use light inline formatting where useful.
- Keep raw ticket descriptions/comments in local context artifacts, outside the HTML. Link PR, source documents, branches, and pinned commits. Preserve run artifacts on success while removing the temporary worktree.
- Keep generated artifacts local. Do not post comments, submit reviews, apply fixes, alter branches, add labels, or modify tracked ignore files.

## Failure handling

- Stop if `git` or `gh` is unavailable or unauthenticated.
- Linear failures do not block the code review. Record the exact failure in `linear_context`.
- If finalization rejects the JSON, fix only the invalid structured output and retry.
- If any step after preparation cannot complete, clean the worktree before returning while
  preserving diagnostic artifacts:

```powershell
python "<package>/skills/mg-pr-review-html/scripts/generate_pr_review.py" cleanup --manifest <manifest-path> --keep-artifacts
```

## Resources

- `references/review-prompt.md`: PR-specific review and writing requirements.
- `references/codex-review-rubric.md`: finding threshold and review behavior.
- `assets/review-output-schema.json`: structured review contract.
- `scripts/generate_pr_review.py`: prepare, finalize, and cleanup workflow.
- `scripts/render_review.py`: self-contained HTML renderer.


## Primer presentation

Use GitHub Primer styling for review HTML, with bundled semantic light/dark tokens and native HTML controls. Follow [Primer design guidance](../mg-review-lab/references/primer-design.md). Preserve offline exports and existing review interactions.

When producing the shared review lab, include an authored Pseudocode tab for every queued PR. Follow [the lab pseudocode contract](../mg-review-lab/references/pseudocode.md), inspecting the pinned code and retaining failure paths and review caveats. Generate through the canonical lab renderer rather than patching HTML.

Preserve historical context dates even when the PR review is newer. No rank is changed by this adapter.

The `validate` command enforces identities, SHAs, hunk/layer references and visual targets. Evidence is not approval.

Top level: `version:1`, `title`, `generated_at`, `snapshot_note`, `prs`, `dependencies`, `provenance`.

Each PR: `key` (owner/repo#number), `repository`, `number`, `url`, `title`, `base_sha`, `head_sha`, `observed_at`, `freshness` (historical/current/stale/unknown), nullable `current_head_sha`, `intent`, `ticket`, `mode`, `risk`, `readiness`, `next_action`, `priority`, `effort`, `reviewers`, `close_candidate`, `requirements`, `findings`, `checks`, `decisions`, `layers`, `files`.

Priority: `level`, `reason`, `basis`, `confidence`. Effort: `band`, `reason`. Reviewer/close recommendations require reason and source URL. Current freshness requires matching reviewed/current heads and a recent provider observation. Rendering does not refresh evidence.

Files: `id`, `path`, `old_path`, `status`, `hunks`, `notice`. Hunks: `id`, old/new starts/counts, `lines` containing `kind` (context/add/delete/meta), nullable old/new line numbers and exact `text`. Layers: `id`, `title`, `summary`, `basis` (authored/structural), `hunk_ids`, `requirement_ids`, `finding_ids`, `check_ids`, `visuals`. Requirements: `id`, `text`, `source_url`, `assessment`, `verification`, `layer_ids`, `check_ids`. Filename matches cannot establish verification. Preserve source conflicts and non-goals.

Visuals have `kind`, `title`, `caption`. Flow/architecture/sequence/state use `nodes:[{id,label,detail,layer_id}]` and `edges:[{from,to,label}]`. Pseudocode uses `before`,`after`, optional `layer_id`. Decision tables use `columns`,`rows`. UI comparisons use embedded image data URIs `before_src`,`after_src` and meaningful `before_alt`,`after_alt`. Author from inspected behavior, not filenames.

Dependencies: `before`,`after` PR keys, `kind`,`confidence`,`summary`,`url`. External keys render as external prerequisites. Only explicit high-confidence blockers/stacks affect automatic order. Importers label heuristic mappings and preserve old evidence.

Browser progress is snapshot-specific. `compare` produces candidates for evidence-based rereview, not automatic fixed findings. Private source text stays outside the HTML.

## Narrative record

Optional `narrative` is bound to base/head and contains authored explanatory text and verified diff targets. See [the narrative guide](narrative.md) for fields, attribution and validation. It does not change review depth, findings, checks or readiness.

`narrative.format_version: 2` adds optional structured `example`, before/after
`pseudocode`, and disclosed `verification` text. Examples and pseudocode target a
validated narrative step through `step_id`. Version 2 without these blocks shows
before/after prose. Missing format version means the legacy flow layout. This does
not change the top-level record version or browser progress identity.

## Review execution

Optional `review_execution` records `base_sha`, `head_sha`, `reviewed_at`, `depth`, and `summary`. Individual checks retain command, status, observed execution and evidence URL. Optional `intent_source_text` preserves full acceptance wording when requirements are grouped. Such requirements set `source_kind: paraphrased`; omit it for formatting-normalized ticket text. description: Triage a queue of related GitHub pull requests, review selected PRs against Linear intent at a risk-proportionate depth, and produce a polished offline HTML dashboard with compact evidence-backed review capsules. # PR Review Queue HTML

Review GitHub pull requests without changing GitHub, Linear, the source checkout, or its active worktree. Produce local, self-contained HTML as the primary deliverable. Never post comments, submit reviews, change labels or branches, update Linear, apply fixes, or launch a nested model process.

## Choose the mode

- `triage`: mandatory first pass for a queue. Gather only enough evidence to assess intent, ticket linkage, change surface, risk, readiness, dependencies, semantic center, and next action.
- `standard`: normal selected-PR review. Validate the behavioral contract, intended scope, semantic center, tests, and actionable introduced findings.
- `deep`: standard review plus wider call-site tracing, richer explanation, diagrams, selected excerpts, and additional proportionate checks. Use only for high-risk or explicitly requested depth.
- `rereview`: compare the last reviewed immutable head SHA with the current head and revisit unresolved findings. Do not rebuild unchanged explanation.

Read [references/modes.md](references/modes.md) for the selected mode. Read [references/data-contract.md](references/data-contract.md) before writing or validating structured review data. For a performance/cache evaluation, also read [references/evaluation.md](references/evaluation.md). **Why:** The GitHub eslint annotator attributes warnings to whoever last touched the line. "Warning-neutral relocation" is not neutral on the PR — the reviewer sees new warnings.

**How to apply:** When a swap/extraction moves lines that carry lint warnings, fix the underlying issue in the same PR instead of preserving the pattern. For `Json` metadata access: narrow with `x !== null && typeof x === "object" && !Array.isArray(x)` — TS then resolves property access natively, no casts. **The exact CI mechanism** (`.github/workflows/ci.yaml`, `lint-changed-files`, verified 2026-07-27): eslint runs on whole changed *files*, but the result goes through `reviewdog -filter-mode=added -fail-level=warning`. So warnings on lines the diff does NOT touch never fail the job — only added/changed lines do. Practical consequence: adding a one-token edit to a file full of pre-existing warnings is safe, and `npx eslint --max-warnings 0 <file>` failing locally is not by itself a CI failure.
